Customer interested in mixing hosted + private pilot for sensitive workloads, wants clear latency SLAs for APAC and cost comparison. Security questions around KMS, audit logs, and data retention. Agreement to run a 1-week pilot and Redwood to send updated SOW/pricing and benchmark plan.
topics: Cost vs latency tradeoffs and quantization profiles
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-01 15:30 UTC | Duration: 48 minutes | Recording: yes
Attendees: Lina Ortega (Redwood AE), Marcus Kim (Redwood SE), Priya Reddy (Head of MLOps, OceanLight), Tom Bennett (CTO), Sara Vang (Security Lead), Diego Morales (Infra), Anna Cho (PM)

[00:00] Lina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. This is Lina from Redwood, se-- we'll go quick. Marcus and I are here to run through renewal options, the APAC/EU burst asks you sent and the private pilot for sovereign data.
[00:22] Tom: Yeah thanks. Um, we want to make sure we don't surprise cost but also need the latency for APAC users — last quarter we saw token lat spikes.
[00:36] Priya: Right, and we'd love to pin down what parts can stay hosted vs what we'd push to private. Sara will, you know, own the security concerns.
[00:47] Marcus: Cool. Quick outline: 1) current usage and projection; 2) proposed uplift tiers and burst pockets; 3) private/VPC pilot scope; 4) benchmarks & SLOs. Feel free to interrupt.
[01:05] Diego: Quick note — our infra team needs the exact whitelists for peering, the last time there was a mismatch and it took two days.
[01:13] Lina: Yep we'll include a network checklist.
[01:18] Tom: Great. Priya, do you want to go over current usage?
[01:25] Priya: Sure. We're running about 1.2B tokens a month on average, peak bursts on month ends closer to 1.9B. Most of that is chat and embeddings for our search assistant. We turned on Redwood cache last quarter, helped, but we're bumping into concurrency limits in APAC.
[01:46] Marcus: When you say concurrency limits, is that request per-second or token-streaming related?
[01:51] Priya: Both. The per-second request rate and the streaming tail latency for long sessions.
[01:59] Marcus: Okay. For APAC we recommend a small dedicated pool + hosted burst fallback. That gives you low tail latency for hot workloads and cost-efficient fallback.
[02:12] Tom: How different is the execution path between hosted and dedicated? We heard something about different quantization and kernel sets.
[02:19] Marcus: Good point — dedicated lets us tune the runtime: optimized kernels, persistent KV cache for long chats, and you can pin a quantization profile. Hosted is more generalized but we've got verified perf profiles in the catalog. You may see ~10-25% delta depending on sequence length.
[02:38] Sara: On the private pilot — our compliance team wants KMS in our cloud region, audit logs retained for 7 years, and role-based access. Does Redwood Private support HSM/KMS integration and long-term logs?
[02:49] Lina: Yes, Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS or HSM; we support audit export to your SIEM and configurable retention. Small caveat: on extremely long retention we recommend S3 lifecycle policies on the customer side to avoid storage surprises.
[03:07] Priya: When you say Redwood Private, do you mean fully on-prem or VPC-hosted private control plane? We want the VPC option first.
[03:15] Marcus: VPC private is the recommended starting point — private control plane with customer-managed networking and optional on‑prem later if needed.
[03:22] Diego: Ok that aligns. For the pilot window, what's provisioning time for a small private cluster?
[03:28] Lina: For VPC option typically 3–5 business days for provisioning once network and certs are exchanged. For full on-prem it's multi-week because of packaging and infra.
[03:37] Anna: Can you clarify the pricing model for a short pilot — any minimum term?
[03:42] Lina: We usually do a pilot rate for a 1-week private pilot — it's an uplift over hosted but we credit it toward the renewal if you commit to a dedicated or private contract within 30 days. We'll include specific numbers in the SOW.
[03:56] Tom: We need the economics — ie cost per 1M tokens under dedicated vs hosted and the burst pricing for APAC/EU.
[04:05] Marcus: We'll put a comparison table in the SOW; rough rule of thumb: dedicated becomes attractive around your current base plus predictable growth. For large burst events, the hybrid model tends to minimize overall spend while hitting latency SLOs.
[04:22] Priya: Also curious about model variants — if we fall back to a cheaper quantized model for non-sensitive requests, can that happen automatically?
[04:31] Marcus: Yes, smart routing policies can automatically route non-sensitive routes to quantized variants. We can also do canary splits. There might be small quality regressions—we should test with your eval suite.
[04:45] Sara: On the security checklist: SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS, audit log exports, data residency — any gotchas? For KMS, do you persist any keys?
[04:58] Marcus: No, with customer KMS we only reference keys — Redwood doesn't store your plaintext keys. For hosted with Redwood-managed KMS, keys are in our control and that's a different compliance posture. We'll map both options in doc.
[05:16] Diego: For the VPC peering test — can we do a dry-run with a small dev cluster?
[05:20] Lina: Absolutely, we recommend a dev staging peering test first. We'll include exact IPs, ports, CIDR ranges in the network checklist.
[05:30] Tom: About SLA, we need tail latency SLOs for APAC — 95th percentile under 400ms for short sequences. Is that reasonable?
[05:39] Marcus: Short sequences, yes we can target that from a dedicated pool in APAC. Hosted might be higher depending on region availability. We'll run benchmarks to validate.
[05:49] Priya: Benchmarks — we need test harness that mirrors our traffic (chat, length distribution). Marcus, can you propose a plan?
[05:56] Marcus: Plan is: 1) you give us a 24-hour representative sample of seq/length distribution; 2) we run three test sweeps across hosted, dedicated APAC pool, and VPC pilot with your quantization profiles; 3) we produce latency/cost per token report. We'll share the harness and scripts.
[06:15] Priya: We can't share PII but can provide anonymized traces.
[06:19] Marcus: Perfect. Anonymized traces are fine.
[06:22] Sara: A quick security red flag: retention for embeddings — we need explicit opt-in for storing embeddings beyond 30 days. Can Redwood configure that per route?
[06:33] Lina: Yes we support route-level retention. For hosted customers you can choose ephemeral caching or persistent. For private it’s fully configurable. We'll document routes and defaults.
[06:44] Tom: On the renewal term — we're leaning toward a 12-month committed uplift with optional quarterly burst top-ups. Is that negotiable?
[06:53] Lina: That's a common approach. We can draft a 12-month base commitment with quarterly top-ups and a clause for region activation windows.
[07:03] Diego: Any special network ports or mTLS cert steps? Last time we tripped on cert chain.
[07:10] Marcus: We'll provide an mTLS handshake doc. For VPC peering, it's standard: BGP optional, mTLS required for control plane. We'll also send a checklist for cert rotation.
[07:23] Priya: Alright, timeline — we want a pilot in mid-March to validate APAC perf before committing. Any showstoppers?
[07:31] Lina: No showstoppers. We just need sign-off on NDA addendum for pilot, network owners, and budget approval.
[07:38] Tom: On the NDA addendum — legal needs that by next week.
[07:42] Lina: We'll route that to legal today.
[07:45] Anna: Can we get a short one-page summary for execs with cost delta and recommended path?
[07:51] Lina: Yes we'll include an exec one-pager in the SOW package.
[07:55] Priya: A question on telemetry — can we get token-level breakdowns per route and per model variant?
[08:02] Marcus: Yes our Console provides token-level breakdown, route dashboards, and tracing. Retention on those metrics is configurable as an add-on.
[08:11] Sara: For audit logs retention 7 years — does that require special provisioning?
[08:15] Marcus: If you want logs exported to your S3 and lifecycle controlled there, we can do that. For hosted long-term retention we'd route via your SIEM. We'll be explicit in the SOW with storage implications.
[08:28] Tom: Ok good. Anything about legal procurement timelines?
[08:32] Lina: Our standard procurement cycle for enterprise sometimes takes 3–6 weeks. For pilots we can do a limited SOW to accelerate.
[08:39] Diego: Can the pilot include a small on‑prem node to test HSM integration?
[08:44] Marcus: Technically yes but that adds provisioning complexity. Recommend starting VPC + KMS in-region, then iterate to HSM.
[08:54] Priya: Sounds reasonable.
[08:57] Lina: Recap — Redwood will: 1) send SOW + exec one-pager with APAC/EU burst pricing and pilot credit; 2) share benchmark plan and infra checklist; 3) produce proposed pilot dates Mar 15–22; 4) route NDA addendum to legal. Customer will: 1) provide anonymized traffic sample; 2) assign network contact for peering; 3) outline SOC2/KMS specifics.
[09:24] Tom: Good — on the SOW include clear crediting of pilot toward final commitment.
[09:29] Lina: Will do.
[09:31] Anna: Quick nit — can we get a compatibility doc for our current authentication (Okta SAML)?
[09:37] Marcus: Yes we integrate with Okta SAML. We'll include steps.
[09:41] Priya: Any blockers we should be aware of?
[09:45] Marcus: Only network and legal timelines. From an infra perspective we can stand up the dev cluster quickly.
[09:52] Sara: On cryptography, please send the KMS integration diagram, we need to ensure keys never leave our region.
[09:59] Lina: We'll get that to you.
[10:02] Diego: One more question — is there an option for per-route retention policies to be enforced automatically on embeddings?
[10:09] Marcus: Yes, we can configure per-route retention and deletion policies — we'll include an example policy.
[10:15] Priya: Thanks. That helps.
[10:18] Lina: Ok thanks everyone — we'll follow up with SOW and the benchmark plan. Expect an email EOD tomorrow.
[10:26] Tom: Thanks Lina.
[10:28] Priya: Thanks all.
[10:30] [meeting ends]

Notes/imperfections: occasional mis-transcribed phrases — e.g., "Redwood Dedi-cat-ed" appears as "Redwood Dedicat-ed" in text, "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash". There was a brief voicemail beep captured at ~00:20 causing a speaker label confusion. Some proper names may be slightly off in speaker tags.

Outcome: Agreement to run 1-week private pilot (VPC) mid-March, Redwood to send SOW, benchmarks & network checklist, customer to provide anonymized traces and network contact.
